title: Developer integration sprint kickoff - auth & env
summary: Kickoff for a 2-week integration sprint: SDK quickstart (Python + TS), auth patterns (API key vs SSO/SAML), environment setup for sandbox and staging, and Optimize recommendations for batching/kv-cache. Agreed pilot: 2-week POC using Redwood hosted with plans to evaluate Dedicated if latency needs persist.
topics: Auth options: API key, SSO/SAML, service principals
Optimize suggestions: batching, caching, quantization recommendations
Security questions: SOC2, KMS, audit logs
next_steps: Priya to send sandbox API key and quickstart repo link by 2025-04-08
Quarry to provide a representative prompt set and 24h traffic profile by 2025-04-10
Ethan to schedule a Dedicated capacity sizing chat if benchmarks exceed 150ms p50 by 2025-04-14
action_items: Priya Nair (Redwood SE) - Share Python + TS quickstart repo, example env files, and a short runbook - due 2025-04-08
Liam O'Connor (Quarry) - Deliver sample prompt set and 3 anonymized records for eval - due 2025-04-10
Sara Kim (Quarry) - Confirm CI secret manager (Vault) integration approach for staging - due 2025-04-11
transcript:
[00:00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Liam: Liam here, lead eng at Quarry.
[00:00:11] Sara: Sara, DevOps.
[00:00:13] Marcus: Marcus, product.
[00:00:16] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya from Redwood, I'll run the demo and help with the SDK bits.
[00:00:22] Ethan: Goal for today — get you unblocked with auth, environment setup, and run a quick python/typescript sample so your engineers can begin the sprint.
[00:00:37] Liam: Sounds good. Our main constraint: PHI-like data in prompts, so we need clear guidance on data residency and KMS, also SSO for non-root access.
[00:00:51] Priya: Totally. We support hosted with isolated projects, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For keys we can do API keys for quickstart, and SAML SSO + RBAC for org access. We also integrate with KMS for key wrapping.
[00:01:12] Sara: Do you have a runbook for CI secrets? We run Hashi Vault in staging.
[00:01:18] Priya: Yes, I'll attach the Vault pattern — set the Redwood API key as a secret and inject into CI as REDWOOD_API_KEY. We'll include example GitHub/GitLab steps.
[00:01:30] Marcus: Can you walk us through the quickstart code? Prefer to see both python and TS.
[00:01:36] Priya: Sure, starting with Python. I have a lightweight snippet. Note — the SDK repo link is in the notes, but here's the flow: pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, import redwood, client = redwood.Client(), call client.generate(...).
[00:01:58] [00:02:00] Priya: (typing) If anyone following, the snippet uses text generation, we show streaming and non-streaming examples. The python SDK supports an async runner and chunked streaming.
[00:02:19] Liam: Any gotchas with env var names across languages? We use a shared env pattern.
[00:02:25] Priya: REDWOOD_API_KEY is consistent. For local dev we recommend .env with dotenv, and for CI use your secrets manager, plus a staging key with lower quotas.
[00:02:36] Ethan: Quick note on roles: create separate API keys per service with scopes — read-only embeddings vs generate. That reduces blast radius.
[00:02:47] Sara: How about SSO? We need SAML, can we do SCIM provisioning?
[00:02:52] Priya: Yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. You'll typically enroll org admins first, then map groups to RBAC roles. We can share the SSO setup doc.
[00:03:08] [00:03:15] Priya: Moving to TypeScript: npm install @redwood-inference/sdk (note: package name in example), set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, import { Client } from '@redwood-inference/sdk', const client = new Client(). Then client.chat.create or client.generate.
[00:03:40] Liam: Ok, demo that live?
[00:03:44] Priya: I'll run a small local example hitting hosted sandbox — please excuse occasional slowness, network at our end.
[00:03:55] [00:04:05] Priya: (runs) Example output: returned tokens, we show token usage breakdown in Console. You can see latency per token and cost estimate.
[00:04:22] Marcus: The Console — can you show where to see per-route latency?
[00:04:26] Priya: Sure, opening the Console — under Observability -> Routes you get p50/p95 token latency, cost per request, and token counts. We'll annotate the route with labels so you can tie it to a microservice.
[00:04:45] [00:05:00] Ethan: A common ask: how to tune for lower cost without hurting quality? Priya can speak to Optimize.
[00:05:07] Priya: Optimize gives suggestions: batching config, prefix/KV caching for repeated context, and recommended quantization for offline models. For hosted we auto-propose batching levels based on your traffic profile. For example, if your average request size is 128 tokens and request inter-arrival is 10 qps, we recommend a 20ms batching window to increase GPU fill.
[00:05:40] Sara: Is batching automatic or manual? We can't afford increased tail latency.
[00:05:45] Priya: It's policy-driven — you choose latency SLOs and Optimize recommends a config. We can do continuous batching with fallback to single-shot if queueing would violate SLOs. So you'll see graceful degradation.
[00:05:59] [00:06:10] Liam: Regarding data — do logs leave our region? We need residency in eu-west-1.
[00:06:15] Priya: Hosted supports region pinning for logs and execution. For stricter requirements we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with regional pools. We also support KMS integration so payloads can be encrypted at rest with your key.
[00:06:32] Marcus: Does Redwood keep prompts for training?
[00:06:35] Ethan: By default, hosted data is not used for model training if you opt-out at the org level; enterprise contracts can include data handling terms. We'll share the data retention and training policy doc.
[00:06:50] [00:07:10] Priya: Back to quickstart: I'll show a small CI pipeline snippet that runs a smoke test: sets REDWOOD_API_KEY, hits the health endpoint, runs a sample generate and ensures a 200 and token_count < threshold.
[00:07:28] Sara: Nice, that'll fit our deploy gates. On quotas — can we have separate quotas per env?
[00:07:33] Priya: Yes, create project keys per environment, each with its own quota. Console allows per-key usage limits.
[00:07:44] Liam: What about embedding pipelines? We do similarity search with vector DB. Which embedding sizes?
[00:07:49] Priya: We have multiple embedding models; you can generate 1536-dim or 1024 depending on model. We'll suggest a model and show cost. Also recommend caching embedding results for static docs to avoid recomputing.
[00:08:06] [00:08:20] Ethan: For the POC, what's success? Liam?
[00:08:23] Liam: Two things: 1) end-to-end request latency under 200ms p50 for our sample prompts, 2) cost per 1k tokens under our target. Also must pass our security checklist.
[00:08:37] Priya: We'll run a benchmark over your prompt set in sandbox and share results. If latency is poor we'll discuss Dedicated sizing.
[00:08:47] [00:09:00] Priya: Quick note about model variants — we have LLM variants with lower VRAM footprints, quantized builds, and fallback to smaller models if the primary is busy. That helps reliability.
[00:09:12] Marcus: How do we route between hosted and Dedicated?
[00:09:16] Priya: Smart routing — policy based. You can route sensitive requests to Dedicated and public ones to hosted. We can show a routing rule example.
[00:09:28] [00:09:40] Priya: Now I'll show the repo structure: examples/python_quickstart, examples/ts_quickstart, docs/auth.md, docs/ci.md. The python example has both sync and async variants.
[00:09:55] [00:10:10] Priya: (reads snippet) Python sync generate: response = client.generate(model='rw-base-1', prompt=..., max_tokens=200). For streaming you attach a callback. Note: the model name in example is a placeholder; actual prod names are in Console.
[00:10:30] Liam: Any common errors you see?
[00:10:33] Priya: 401 from wrong key, CORS for browser usage if you use client-side keys (we recommend server-side proxy or short-lived tokens), and mismatch of model name between Console and SDK causing 404-like errors. Also some folks confuse KV cache vs Redis — our KV cache is in-memory prefix cache at the runtime layer.
[00:10:56] [00:11:15] Sara: Browser usage — we plan a JS front-end. What's the recommended pattern?
[00:11:20] Priya: Use a short-lived session token minted by your backend — backend uses REDWOOD_API_KEY to create a session with limited privileges and TTL, then front-end uses that. Avoid embedding long-lived API keys in client code.
[00:11:35] Liam: Can we do role-based access per route?
[00:11:38] Ethan: Yes, RBAC is supported; map groups to roles and create route-level policies. We can demo a sample policy file.
[00:11:48] [00:12:05] Priya: I'll run a quick embed example: send a doc, get embedding vector, push to your vector DB (we have connectors for Pinecone, Milvus, others). We'll show the latency and token counts.
[00:12:25] Marcus: For the Optimize recommendations, can they be exported? We want to track changes in our infra repo.
[00:12:30] Priya: Optimize suggestions can be exported as JSON or an infra snippet. We'll add it to a PR for review.
[00:12:40] [00:13:00] Priya: Running a live micro-benchmark now against hosted sandbox: 100 requests, sample traffic. (observes) p50 ~ 180ms, p95 ~ 420ms — remember sandbox is multi-tenant and somewhat noisy.
[00:13:22] Liam: That's promising. If our real traffic is stricter, how does Dedicated sizing work?
[00:13:28] Priya: We'll model expected concurrent requests and avg tokens and propose a GPU pool. For low-latency we recommend batching with aggressive KV cache for prefix-heavy workloads.
[00:13:45] Sara: Do you support client-side certs for mutual TLS? We have strict network policies.
[00:13:50] Priya: For Private deployments we support mutual TLS and custom network appliance integration. For hosted, we use TLS and can do private peering.
[00:14:02] [00:14:20] Ethan: Let's address compliance: SOC2, ISO, audit logs, retention. Priya, quick summary?
[00:14:25] Priya: Redwood is SOC2 Type II, we have ISO docs available on request. Audit logs are available in Console and can be exported to your SIEM. We'll include the compliance packet in the repo we share.
[00:14:41] Marcus: Great. About billing — can staging be limited to a monthly cap?
[00:14:46] Priya: Yes, per-project quotas and per-key spend caps are available. We can set alerts and automatic throttles.
[00:14:55] [00:15:15] Priya: Now a quick walkthrough of error handling in the SDK: client.errors has typed exceptions, and the TS SDK returns a status code and an error body. We'll show sample retry logic using exponential backoff and idempotency tokens for safe retries.
[00:15:40] Liam: Any sample retry code for the python SDK?
[00:15:44] Priya: Yes, we'll drop that in the examples folder - typical pattern is retry on 429/5xx with jittered backoff, and don't retry on 400/401.
[00:15:58] [00:16:10] Ethan: Ok let's capture the sprint plan — two weeks, sandbox integration, then benchmark and check-in.
[00:16:16] Marcus: Timeline is fine. Any blockers?
[00:16:20] Sara: Need access to the sandbox key and the quickstart repo.
[00:16:24] Priya: We'll provide both.
[00:16:28] [00:16:40] Priya: One more demo: show Console route tagging — you can create a route named company-search and attach a model, set a per-route quota, and attach an A/B rollout to test an updated model.
[00:16:57] Liam: Useful. We do canary deploys for model updates.
[00:17:01] Priya: Console supports canary rollouts and automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to eval suites.
[00:17:12] [00:17:30] Ethan: Any questions on evals?
[00:17:32] Marcus: We'll want to hook our internal eval metrics (bleu-like scores and domain-specific checks) into Redwood. Can we push eval results?
[00:17:39] Priya: Yes, you can push eval results into Console or pull them via API. We also support scheduled eval runs against a prompt set.
[00:17:51] [00:18:10] Priya: Going back to auth: I'll show SAML setup steps briefly — metadata exchange, SP-initiated flow, group mapping. SCIM is optional but recommended for larger orgs.
[00:18:27] Sara: For SAML, do you support attribute-mapping for department?
[00:18:31] Priya: Yes attribute mapping to roles is supported.
[00:18:36] [00:18:55] Priya: Quick note on session tokens for browser flows: short TTL (5-15m), scope-limited, rotate frequently. We'll include sample code for minting session tokens server-side.
[00:19:08] Liam: Any unexpected costs from session tokens?
[00:19:12] Priya: Session tokens are free; usage billed on actual inference tokens and embeddings.
[00:19:20] [00:19:40] Priya: Now I'll demonstrate a small optimize recommendation export: suggests enabling KV cache for route company-search, batching window 25ms, and quantizing model to int8 for staging.
[00:19:58] Marcus: Quantization in staging — do we see regression risks?
[00:20:02] Priya: Slight drop in quality for some tasks, Optimize ties to an eval set so it will flag regressions. You can auto-promote if quality thresholds are met.
[00:20:18] [00:20:40] Ethan: Let's talk monitoring — did you want SNMP or Slack alerts?
[00:20:45] Sara: Slack and PagerDuty.
[00:20:48] Priya: We have built-in alerting into Slack and PD, and webhook sinks for custom integrations.
[00:20:58] [00:21:15] Liam: Are there SDK examples for our Node microservices and Python backend?
[00:21:19] Priya: Yes, examples cover Flask/FastAPI and Express/Koa. We'll include a small proxy pattern for safe front-end usage.
[00:21:31] [00:21:50] Priya: Time check — we have ~30 minutes left. Any deep dive requests now?
[00:21:56] Liam: Could Priya look at our sample prompt set after the call and suggest caching points?
[00:22:01] Priya: Absolutely, send them over and we'll annotate with caching and batching tips.
[00:22:08] [00:22:25] Priya: I'll also drop a sample bench harness you can run locally that hits the sandbox endpoint with concurrency and token distribution to simulate prod.
[00:22:34] Marcus: Will we get a summary repo with all docs?
[00:22:38] Ethan: Yes, we'll create a repo for the sprint with README, quickstarts, security packet, and the bench harness.
[00:22:48] [00:23:05] Priya: One more note: if you decide to go Private for residency, there's an onboarding lead time for VPC connectivity — typically 3-4 weeks. Dedicated is faster to get GPUs but may require contract.
[00:23:22] Liam: Good to know. Our timeline aims to decide after the 2-week POC.
[00:23:28] [00:23:50] Priya: Demo wrap-up — I'll paste code examples in chat now. (pastes) Python example shows API call and simple retry wrapper. TS example shows chat streaming via EventSource.
[00:24:10] Marcus: small quibble — EventSource had some CORS annoyances previously.
[00:24:15] Priya: Use server-sent events via a server proxy or web sockets via our SDK; we have examples for both.
[00:24:30] [00:24:50] Ethan: Ok let's capture final next steps: repo, sandbox key, prompt set, bench run.
[00:24:57] Priya: I'll send sandbox creds and link to repo after the call.
[00:25:10] Liam: When can we do the midpoint check-in?
[00:25:14] Ethan: How about 2025-04-14 at the same time?
[00:25:18] Liam: Works.
[00:25:22] Marcus: Thx all.
[00:25:25] Priya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and the action items.
[00:25:30] Ethan: Meeting adjourned.

Note: transcript contains occasional ASR mistakes (e.g., 'KV cash' vs KV cache, 'kube-ness' vs Kubernetes) and some speaker overlap entries.
